cards.explanation: The answer is False. Pilate asks, "Are You the King of the Jews?" and Jesus answers, "You have said so…" (Mark 15:2) He never tells Pilate He isn't. Keep an ear out for how short that answer is, friends, because Jesus doesn't say much to Pilate in this passage.

The answer is that Pilate is amazed. The text says, "…to Pilate’s amazement, Jesus made no further reply." (Mark 15:5) Pilate had just pointed at a mountain of charges and asked for an answer, and he got silence. I think I'd be staring too, friends.

The answer is that they ask Pilate to keep his custom. "…the crowd went up and began asking Pilate to keep his custom." (Mark 15:8) That custom was to release a prisoner of their choosing at the feast (Mark 15:6). The crowd is asking him to do what he always does, friends. That's the ask.

The answer is "stir up." "…the chief priests stirred up the crowd to have him release Barabbas to them instead." (Mark 15:11) Barabbas was the man imprisoned with the rebels who had committed murder (Mark 15:7). The crowd got a push, friends, and it came from the chief priests.

The answer is "Crucify Him." "And they shouted back, 'Crucify Him!'" (Mark 15:13) Pilate had asked what to do with the One they call the King of the Jews, and that's the crowd's answer. I think this is a heavy moment, friends, so let's let it be heavy.

The answer is False. Pilate asks, "Why? What evil has He done?" and the crowd doesn't go quiet. Mark says, "they shouted all the louder, 'Crucify Him!'" (Mark 15:14). It's the same two words again, friends. The crowd's answer just got louder.

The answer is True. Mark says, "…wishing to satisfy the crowd, Pilate released Barabbas to them." (Mark 15:15) Barabbas was the man imprisoned with the rebels who had committed murder (Mark 15:7). The text gives us Pilate's reason, friends, and it's the crowd.

The answer is a crown of thorns. The soldiers "…twisted together a crown of thorns, and set it on His head." (Mark 15:17) They also dressed Him in a purple robe. I think this part of the passage is a hard one to read, friends, so let's read it slowly.

The answer is "Hail, King of the Jews." "They began to salute Him: 'Hail, King of the Jews!'" (Mark 15:18) Pilate had used the title King of the Jews when he questioned Jesus (Mark 15:2). Here the soldiers use it in their salute, friends, along with the robe and the crown.

The answer is False. Mark says, "After they had mocked Him, they removed the purple robe and put His own clothes back on Him." (Mark 15:20) So the robe doesn't stay on, friends. His own clothes go back on Him. Then they led Him out to crucify Him.
